title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
subtitle: Milanese braised veal shin with gremolata
excerpt: The great Milanese braise: cross-cut veal shin (osso buco means 'bone with a hole') slow-cooked in white wine, stock, and vegetables until the meat collapses and the marrow in the central bone melts into the braising liquid, then finished with a sharp gremolata of lemon, parsley, and garlic.

recipe.sourceNotes: Osso buco alla Milanese is the definitive dish of Milanese cuisine, dating to the nineteenth century. The name describes the cut: cross-sections of veal shin containing the marrow-filled bone (osso = bone, buco = hole). The dish is traditionally served with saffron risotto alla Milanese, one of the few accepted accompaniments in authentic Milanese cooking. The defining finish is the gremolata, a mixture of raw lemon zest, flat-leaf parsley, and garlic added at the last moment to cut through the richness of the braise. The original recipe uses white wine (not the tomato-enriched version common outside Italy), and the soffritto of onion, celery, and carrot should remain pale. The marrow in the bone is traditionally eaten with a small spoon and is considered the great prize of the dish.

content.text: Tie a length of kitchen string around each piece of veal shin to hold the meat to the bone during braising. The braising liquid should come no more than halfway up the veal; too much liquid produces a stew rather than a braise. The gremolata is added off the heat at the very last moment; it must not cook or it loses its sharp, fresh quality.

items.preparation: 4 cross-cut veal shin pieces, each 4 cm thick (use beef shin if veal unavailable)

content.text: Season the shin pieces and dust lightly with flour. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the shin on both sides until deeply coloured. Remove. Cook the soffritto (onion, celery, carrot) in the same pot over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Return the veal. Add the wine and let it reduce by half. Add the stock, bay, and thyme. The liquid should come halfway up the meat. Cover and braise in the oven at 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3 for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is tender and the marrow is melting.

Mix the parsley, lemon zest, and 1 minced garlic clove to make the gremolata. Remove the casserole from the oven. Scatter the gremolata over the veal and serve immediately with saffron risotto or polenta.
